Rom 2:15), the natural law', quoting Thomas (In duo praecepta caritatis): 'nothing other than the light of understanding infused in us by God ...' Extracted verbatim from the exact fetched response.

passages.context: VS 40-45: rightful autonomy and its limits ('the autonomy of reason cannot mean that reason itself creates values and moral norms', n. 40); 'participated theonomy' (n. 41); natural law named from the reason proper to human nature (n. 42, quoting ST I-II q. 91 a. 2); the eternal law in Augustine and Thomas, natural law as 'the human expression of God's eternal law' (n. 43, quoting Dignitatis humanae 3); Leo XIII, Libertas praestantissimum, on natural law as the eternal law implanted in rational beings (n. 44); the New Law and the unity of God's law (n. 45). Extracted verbatim from the exact fetched response.

work.description: John Paul II's encyclical of 6 August 1993 on fundamental questions of the Church's moral teaching, addressed by numbered paragraph; its second chapter treats freedom and law, including natural law as participated theonomy (nn. 35-53).
